import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_movies = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_94_0
df_ratings = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0) # Source3_94_1
df_users = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)   # Source3_94_2

# Step 1: Join ratings with users on user_id to get sex for each rating
df_ratings_users = pd.merge(df_ratings, df_users[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Aggregate ratings by movie_id and sex to get average rating per sex per movie
avg_ratings_by_sex = df_ratings_users.groupby(['movie_id', 'sex'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Step 3: Pivot the sex column to get separate columns for 'F' and 'M' average ratings
pivot_ratings = avg_ratings_by_sex.pivot(index='movie_id', columns='sex', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot_ratings = pivot_ratings.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Step 4: Join with movies table to get movie titles
df_target = pd.merge(pivot_ratings, df_movies[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema: ['movie_id', 'title', 'F', 'M']
df_target = df_target[['movie_id', 'title', 'F', 'M']]

# Step 6: Ensure correct data types
df_target['movie_id'] = df_target['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_target['title'] = df_target['title'].astype(str)
df_target['F'] = df_target['F'].astype(float)
df_target['M'] = df_target['M'].astype(float)

# Step 7: Write the result to the specified CSV file path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 as instructed
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source0 on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Create columns F and M: average rating by sex per movie
# Filter ratings by sex and aggregate mean rating per movie_id and title
# We group by movie_id and title (leftmost non-float unique keys)

# Compute mean rating for females (sex == 'F')
f_ratings = joined_all[joined_all["sex"] == "F"].groupby(["movie_id", "title"])["rating"].mean().rename("F")

# Compute mean rating for males (sex == 'M')
m_ratings = joined_all[joined_all["sex"] == "M"].groupby(["movie_id", "title"])["rating"].mean().rename("M")

# Combine F and M ratings into one DataFrame
result = pd.concat([f_ratings, m_ratings], axis=1).reset_index()

# Write output to the specified path
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
